ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 31142); Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 289, 292 and 317; National Tax Act; Criminal Proceeds Concealment Regulation Act; Local Tax Act and Education Tax Act; FATF Recommendations as implemented by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Corporate Registration Certificate (parent entity and Korean Chusik Hoesa registration extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent registry in the jurisdiction of origin; for Korea, the District Court Registry Office under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member state: notarize or certify the registry copy, then obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority of that state (e.g., Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Secretary of State, or Attorney-General's Department); do not apply for consular legalization. Non-member state: notarize, authenticate through the state's foreign ministry, then legalize at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate with consular jurisdiction. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (parent entity and Korean Chusik Hoesa)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or registrar of corporations in the jurisdiction of origin; for Korea, the Supreme Court of Korea electronic registry extract office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing state belongs to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain a certified copy and an Apostille from the state's competent authority; no consular authentication is required. If the issuing state is not an Apostille member, notarize the certificate, have it authenticated by the state's ministry of foreign affairs, and then present it to the Republic of Korea consulate for legalization. Do not use Apostille and consular legalization in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing Korean counsel and the intended resident director to incorporate a Chusik Hoesa and open bank accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or corporate secretary of the foreign parent, certified by a notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signatures must be notarized by a notary public in the country of origin. For Apostille member states, apply for an Apostille from the competent national authority and do not consular legalize. For non-member states, follow notarization, foreign ministry authentication, and Korean consular legalization in that order only. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes; never combine them for one document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Articles of Incorporation of the Korean Chusik Hoesa and chartered constitutional documents of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of execution for certified true copies; for the Korean entity, a Korean notary public who has certified the Korean-language articles
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For foreign parent constitutional documents: notarize and then follow either the Apostille route for Apostille Convention states or the consular legalization route for non-member states. The certified Korean articles of incorporation do not require a separate origin-state legalization if they are executed in Korea; they will be apostilled by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs only if needed for outbound use. Never chain a foreign Apostille with Korean consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign parent and intended Korean Chusik Hoesa account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank in the jurisdiction of origin, signed by a branch manager or compliance officer on bank letterhead
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Have the bank officer's signature and corporate capacity notarized. If the bank is located in an Apostille state, obtain an Apostille on the notarized letter from that state's competent authority; no consular legalization is required. If the bank is in a non-Apostille state, follow notarization, foreign ministry authentication, and Korean consular legalization. Many Korean banks will also require the issuing bank to send an independent SWIFT or e-mail confirmation to the Korean account-opening bank. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, shareholders, directors, supervisors, power-of-attorney holders, authorized signatories, and high-volume automated dropshipping merchant counterparties must be screened before incorporation against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, Korea's designated persons and warning listings maintained by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, and global PEP databases covering domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates. Korean counsel must obtain the full beneficial-ownership chain, verify source of wealth for any PEP or sanctions alert, review adverse media and shell-company indicators, and apply enhanced due diligence before any Stripe or PayPal merchant account is filed. The same screening must be refreshed at the time of bank account opening and monitored on an ongoing basis for trade-based money-laundering, refund abuse, and layered dropshipping settlement flows.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-REGISTER; ireg.scourt.go.kr) for corporate trade-name search, reservation, and registration; Hometax (hometax.go.kr) for subsequent business registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean statutory practice requires a trade name that is expressed in Korean orthography, with a mandatory four-tier structure: distinctive brand element, descriptive business-objective element, optional distinguishing marker, and the legal-form suffix Chusik Hoesa for a stock corporation. Foreign names must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul and may have a parallel romanized English trade name; the registry will check similarity against both Hangul and Latin-script registered names. All official filings with the Korean court registry must be in Korean, and English translations are accepted only as evidentiary annexes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a name rejection, the applicant should first obtain the written rejection reason from the registry office, correct any similarity, transliteration, or prohibited-token defect, and file an immediate appeal with the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days from service of the rejection. The appeal must state the rejected name, the grounds of objection to the registry's refusal, and evidence showing there is no identical or confusingly similar registered trade name. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, the written approval of the relevant ministry or regulator must be attached. If based on similarity, a notarized consent letter from the prior trade-name holder may be submitted. A fresh reservation or an extension request must be filed before the current 30-day window expires; failure to appeal within the statutory period extinguishes the name and requires a new filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is likely to be rejected for the dropshipping industry. The National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for business registration and value-added tax invoicing, and Korean banks applying the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions require an actual office inspection and evidence of commercial substance before opening a corporate account. A serviced office with a dedicated lease, meeting room, and visible company signboard may be acceptable if the automated dropshipping entity can demonstrate operational presence, transaction records, and management access. A virtual address alone, with no staff or director presence, is strongly disfavored and will almost certainly be rejected by the local tax office and the bank's AML compliance team.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: Medium (30-40%) for a newly formed automated dropshipping Chusik Hoesa operating from a serviced office during the first year. Inspection checklist for unannounced municipal tax or registry visits: (1) company signboard mounted at the registered office; (2) lease agreement, rent receipts, utility bills, and internet service contracts matching the registered address; (3) business registration certificate and corporate registry extract available on-site; (4) desks, computer terminals, and drop-shipping order management systems accessible; (5) director or delegated employee presence during ordinary business hours; (6) bank statements, invoices, and shipping/returns records for automated settlement flows; (7) documentation of e-commerce platform contractual relationships. If two or more indicators are missing, authorities may treat the office as sham and impose penalties, refuse VAT invoicing, or cancel the business registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 289 (matters to be stated in the Articles of Incorporation), 291 (notarization of the Articles of Incorporation), 295 (payment of share subscription price), 317 (registration of incorporation), 318 (effect of incorporation registration), and 329 (capital and par value); Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 4 to 6 (foreign investment reporting and registration); Value-Added Tax Act Article 8 (business registration); Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce Article 12 (mail-order sales declaration); Personal Information Protection Act Articles 29 to 31 (personal information processing and the designation of a privacy officer); Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Transactions Reports Act for bank onboarding.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the local District Court of the Republic of Korea having territorial jurisdiction over the registered head office; electronic filing through the IROS Internet Registration System of the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank certificate of payment of subscription price, written consents of initial directors and statutory auditor, and supporting identification documents; the court assesses registration tax at 0.4 percent of issued capital plus local education surtax and a court filing fee, rather than a flat government fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None required by law. The former statutory minimum paid-in capital of KRW 50,000,000 for a Chusik Hoesa was abolished by the December 2012 amendment to the Commercial Act. A company may be incorporated with any stated capital, provided that the full subscription price for every allotted and issued share is deposited into a Korean bank subscription account before the incorporation registration application is filed with the competent District Court. There is no blocked escrow account under Korean company law; the subscription deposit cannot be withdrawn by the promoters before successful registration, and if incorporation fails, the deposit is refunded to the subscribers. After registration, the deposit is released into the corporation's operating bank account. Financial institutions and payment processors such as Stripe and PayPal may impose contractual minimum balance or operating capital expectations, but that is not a government capital blockade rule.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the First Board of Directors of the Company (Chusik Hoesa), as follows: (1) CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The issued share capital of the Company shall be and is hereby fixed at Korean Won [INSERT AMOUNT IN KRW], divided into [INSERT NUMBER] ordinary shares having a par value of [INSERT PAR VALUE IN KRW] per share. The subscription price of all issued shares has been paid in full into a subscription deposit account opened with [INSERT BANK NAME] in the name of the promoters or the Company, and the bank certificate of payment evidencing the same shall be attached to the incorporation registration file, all pursuant to Articles 295 and 317 of the Commercial Act. (2) REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered head office of the Company is hereby adopted as [INSERT FULL ADDRESS], Republic of Korea. The Representative Director is authorized to execute and deliver any lease, landlord consent, or registered-office notice, to accept legal process on behalf of the Company at such address, and to complete the Business Registration filing with the National Tax Service. The registered office is an administrative address only, and no industrial facility or warehouse will be installed at such address. (3) STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following persons are hereby elected and appointed to hold office immediately following incorporation: [INSERT NAME] as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: Home Tax Service (Hometax) at hometax.go.kr; export customs declarations are processed through the Korea Customs Service via the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Any foreign non-resident enterprise that engages in a Korean VAT-taxable supply chain or establishes a taxable nexus in the Republic of Korea must apply for a Business Registration Number (BRN) with the National Tax Service (NTS) through the Home Tax Service (HTS) portal or at the competent district tax office. The application is made on the statutory business registration application for a non-resident or foreign corporation and must be accompanied by (i) a certified copy of the articles of incorporation and certificate of corporate existence in the home jurisdiction; (ii) the foreign enterprise's tax identification number; (iii) documents evidencing the appointment of directors and, where required, a domestic tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes; (iv) preliminary financial statements or a start-up declaration showing the intended taxable supply activity; and (v) a power of attorney when filed through a licensed tax agent or legal representative. After verification, the NTS issues a 10-digit BRN that simultaneously functions as the Korean TIN and VAT identification number. A foreign non-resident supplier without a domestic place of business may use the simplified non-resident electronic-service registration procedure in the Home Tax Service and must obtain a BRN before issuing Korean tax invoices or filing VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korean tax law imposes entity-level corporate income tax and VAT without elective check-the-box classification. Hybrid mismatch rules are implemented under the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination and do not create a tax classification election. No pass-through election is available for a Chusik Hoesa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a domestic place of business or fixed establishment, mandatory VAT registration applies from the first Korean taxable supply with no general turnover exemption. For foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic or digital services, compulsory VAT registration is triggered when the annual Korean B2C supply is estimated to exceed KRW 300,000,000 in the current calendar year or actual Korean B2C supply exceeded KRW 300,000,000 in the preceding calendar year. Imported goods remain subject to Korean customs VAT at importation regardless of seller registration status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered persons in Korea are required to issue statutory Korean tax invoices and to participate in the NTS electronic tax invoice system through the Home Tax Service portal or NTS-approved e-invoicing service providers. For B2B supplies, electronic tax invoices are mandatory and must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following issuance; a digital acceptance and audit-trail record is created in the Home Tax Service. Korea does not operate a continuous fiscal pre-clearance stamping regime, but the NTS applies mandatory e-invoicing, anti-fraud cross-matching of purchase and sales documentation, and periodic aggregate VAT data reporting through statutory VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, exports of goods are zero-rated where the goods are shipped or transported from Korea to a foreign country, ownership passes to a non-resident buyer, and the export customs declaration is accepted by the Korea Customs Service. Qualifying offshore services and certain international transport services may also be zero-rated. In an automated dropshipping model, the Korean entity may zero-rate only the export supply where it actually exports the goods from Korea to the foreign customer; if goods are sourced from overseas fulfillment centers and never enter Korea, the transaction is not a Korean domestic VAT supply and must be excluded from the Korean VAT return rather than zero-rated. The taxpayer must maintain an auditable chain from foreign order, purchase order, supplier invoice, transportation documentation, export clearance, and foreign exchange repatriation to substantiate the zero-rating claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service, including the UNI-PASS export clearance record and export reference number
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the goods, quantity, value, and foreign destination
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing consignment to the non-resident buyer
Purchase order or sales contract from the non-resident buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or export proceeds collection confirmation issued by a foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of the overseas sales proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS may audit export zero-rating claims within the statutory five-year assessment period. If the mandatory export documentation is incomplete, inconsistent, or falsified, the NTS will claw back the zero-rated VAT by reassessing VAT at the standard 10% rate, disallow any associated input VAT refund or credit, and impose statutory penalty taxes for under-reported tax, unlawful or unfounded tax invoices, fraudulent refunds, and delayed payment. Fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating can attract an aggravated penalty of up to 40% of the tax in arrears, additional interest for each period of delay, customs penalties under the Customs Act, and criminal referral for tax evasion or document forgery. The Korea Customs Service may also impose separate penalty taxes for irregularities in export declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with practitioner-level supervision through Foreign Exchange Banks and the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIN).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a managed free-floating exchange-rate regime for the Korean won. Current-account transactions, including trade settlement and service payments, are effectively liberalized and may be executed through Foreign Exchange Banks with minimal documentary checks. Capital-account transactions, by contrast, remain subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, requiring prior declaration, reporting, or approval depending on the nature and size of the flow. There is no statutory surrender requirement for export proceeds; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign-currency accounts, but amounts must be repatriated to Korea within the statutory deadline. Dividend and profit remittances by a Chusik Hoesa require audited financial statements, corporate income tax clearance, and regulatory proof that the foreign direct investment was properly notified and certified. In the dropshipping context, the absence of physical import/export customs declarations is a major hurdle, as cross-border settlement through Stripe and PayPal often lacks the supporting trade documentation required by Korean FX dealers. Consequently, treasury planning must align every inward payment to an underlying declared trade or service transaction, and every outward vendor payment must be mapped to an approved import or service contract. This makes the convertibility assessment operationally convertible but administratively heavy, requiring a licensed local banking relationship for currency conversion and remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received within one year from the date of shipment for general exports, extendable up to one additional year with the approval of the relevant Foreign Exchange Bank. No mandatory conversion ratio is imposed; proceeds may be retained in a designated foreign currency account, but must be repatriated to a domestic Foreign Exchange Bank in an amount equivalent to the export invoice, with reported collection under FEIN.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Investment Registration and Basic Operational KRW Current Account
Capital Escrow Account, KRW Operational Current Account, and Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account
Capital Escrow Account, KRW Operational Current Account, and Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary settlement rail. South Korea requires any entity performing cross-border money transfer or foreign exchange brokerage services to be licensed as a foreign exchange business under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or Revolut have no legal standing to open local Korean bank accounts for a Chusik Hoesa, cannot participate in domestic KRW clearing through BOK-Wire+, and are not recognized depositories for capital registration, FX declaration, or tax payment purposes. They may be used only as ancillary payment aggregation tools for Stripe or PayPal settlement, and any funds swept to such an EMI must be immediately routed to a Tier-1 Korean Foreign Exchange Bank for formal FEIN reporting and tax compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and bank CDD policies, at least one authorized signatory, typically the statutory director or a co-operating director, must physically appear at the chosen bank branch for identity verification and signing ceremony. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted, although some banks may consider a notarized and apostilled power of attorney plus a live audio-video verification interview if the principal is a recognized non-resident investor. In practice, a fully foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa should plan for an in-branch interview of the appointed representative and preparation of certified Korean-language translations of all corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident individual or corporate shareholders with opaque ultimate beneficial ownership, especially when control lacks a clear local nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certified copy of the corporate registry certificate, complete shareholder register, beneficial ownership chart through each natural person, certified copies of passports, proof of residential address for all shareholders and directors, source-of-wealth evidence including tax returns and audited financial statements, strategic bank references from the shareholder's home jurisdiction, and a signed declaration confirming no politically exposed person status unless disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionately high volume of micro-credit-card transactions flowing from Stripe and PayPal without matching customs declarations or physical import documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of aggregate settlement statements from Stripe and PayPal, daily order-level transaction ledger, supplier purchase orders, final-mile carrier tracking numbers, end-consumer invoices, refund and chargeback logs, logistics contracts, and any customs clearances or e-commerce import facilitation records that substantiate the automated dropshipping trade pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential third-party payment pass-through or unlicensed money transmission exposure caused by collecting consumer payments and later disbursing to foreign suppliers after a delay.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written treasury and payment-flow policy, supplier KYC files with identification documents, underlying dropshipping agreements, commission-invoice evidence showing the entity earns a commercial margin rather than a fee-for-transfer, real-time transaction monitoring architecture, AML compliance manual, independent compliance audit report, and contractual proof that suppliers fulfill on the entity's behalf.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected future dividend or capital-account remittance to non-resident shareholders without verified foreign direct investment registration or capital verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foreign Investment Notification certificate obtained through KOTRA or the Foreign Exchange Bank, proof of remittance into the capital escrow account, certified capital verification report, external audited financial statements, corporate income tax assessment and payment receipts, withholding tax certificates for any proposed dividends, board resolution authorizing distribution, and confirmation from the local certified tax accountant that profit remittance rules are satisfied.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share-subscription capital from non-resident shareholders must be routed as a formal foreign direct investment. The entity must file a pre-notification under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act through KOTRA or the designated Foreign Exchange Bank, open a capital escrow account at the Tier-1 Korean bank, receive the inward remittance via SWIFT MT103 using the purpose code corresponding to equity capital contribution from a foreign direct investor, and then perform statutory capital verification. The foreign currency must be converted into KRW through the receiving bank at the market rate, and the resulting KRW funds are credited to the entity's operational current account only after the foreign investment registration certificate is issued. All references in the payment order must cite the Foreign Investment Notification number and the corporate legal name of the Chusik Hoesa to avoid rejection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier payments outside Korea, the entity should primarily use SWIFT MT103 for direct wire settlement when no documentary credit is required. Commercial letters of credit opened by the Tier-1 Korean bank via MT700 are recommended for high-value purchases that require master-document control. Documentary Collections can be used for consignment or scheduled payments with the ability to attach commercial invoices, packing lists, and bills of lading. All outbound disbursements must reference the underlying purchase order, import declaration, or service contract, and must be reported through FEIN to ensure a complete audit trail for foreign exchange and tax authorities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts for maturities up to one year, extendable to five years with documented real-trade exposure, contracted directly with a licensed Korean Foreign Exchange Bank.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in Korean won permitted only to the extent executed by offshore branches or overseas counterparties approved by the Korean authorities, and never used without a corresponding underlying trade or investment exposure.

Cross-currency swaps and interest-rate-currency swaps entered into by the Chusik Hoesa for hedging foreign-currency borrowings or long-term cross-border receivable balances, subject to the bank's internal risk committee and FEIN reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT) and Local Income Tax Surtax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea via the HomeTax electronic filing portal; the associated local income tax surcharge is allocated to the resident local government (Si/Gun/Gu)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending December 31, the return must be filed by March 31 of the following year; one additional month (until April 30) may be obtained by filing an extension request before March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Framework Act on National Taxes: 20% negligence penalty on underpaid tax if filed without payment, 10% if corrected within the voluntary disclosure period; interest at 0.022% per day (approx. 8.03% annually). Persistent non-filing results in tax authority collection procedures (property seizure, credit card payment suspension, and registration of overdue arrears); repeated severe delinquency may lead to compulsory winding-up and strike-off of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements (if statutory threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART system (Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the annual general meeting of shareholders approving the financial statements; because the AGM must be held by March 31 for calendar-year companies, the DART filing is due by April 14 unless the AGM was earlier.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million (approx. USD 7,500); failure or false filing can trigger penalties under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, revocation or suspension of audit-related benefits, and criminal liability for responsible officers. The FSS may also issue corrective orders mandating audit and re-filing within a fixed period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Enterprise Annual Report (for foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa with 10% or greater foreign holding or invested capital over KRW 100 million)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Foreign Investment Support System (FISS) or via Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) delegated desks
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual report due by March 31 for the preceding calendar year; initial foreign investment declaration must be made within 30 days after share subscription/payment.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to KRW 2 million (approx. USD 1,500) for late or inaccurate filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; repeated omissions may result in administrative order for correction and adverse effect on foreign investor status (loss of tax-exemption or protection benefits).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and Statutory Business Book Update (including registration of any share transfers in the shareholder register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial registry with local district court jurisdiction (for registration of shareholder transfers / director changes) and the company's head office for maintenance of the shareholder register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (i.e., by March 31 for calendar-year companies); share transfer entries and related new balances must be recorded in the register at the latest 30 days after transfer notification.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM within the statutory period exposes directors to administrative fines up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,700) under the Korean Commercial Act; non-update of shareholder register may prevent a transfer from being enforceable against the company and can result in fines for inaccurate registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa is subject to mandatory independent CPA audit if at the end of the fiscal year it has total assets of KRW 12 billion or more (approximately USD 9 million), or if it is a listed company. Additional criteria include (i) unlisted companies with annual revenue of KRW 30 billion or more combined with total assets of KRW 7 billion or more; (ii) companies with 100 or more employees and total assets above KRW 5 billion; or (iii) companies designated as public-interest entities or required by the Financial Services Commission. A company falling below these thresholds may nevertheless be audited on a voluntary basis, and any audit must be performed by an authorized certified public accountant registered under Korean law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) as adopted by the Financial Supervisory Service for companies subject to mandatory audit; non-audited small and medium corporations may prepare financial statements under the Korean Small and Medium Enterprise Accounting Standards (K-SME GAAP), but must reconcile to K-IFRS if they later exceed audit thresholds. Corporate tax adjustments follow the Korean Corporate Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not mandate a public annual UBO confirmation statement for ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. However, under the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Information (AML Act), the company must (1) identify and verify beneficial owners each time a client relationship or transaction is established and whenever a change occurs; (2) record changes in beneficial ownership (direct/indirect shareholding of 10% or more or effective control) in the shareholder register within 30 days of the transfer; (3) submit a beneficial-owner confirmation report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) when a transaction exceeds KRW 30 million (approx. USD 22,000) or when red flags appear; and (4) confirm and update UBO records on an annual basis during the corporate tax filing cycle so that the NTS may cross-check material shareholders. For foreign investors, any change in foreign shareholding above the 10% threshold or investment amount exceeding KRW 100 million must be reported to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of the event, with an annual FDI status report due by March 31.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 1,200 per year for a standard registered agent and office arrangement in Seoul or a provincial city; fees cover registered address, mail forwarding, and basic corporate secretary support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 for an SME Chusik Hoesa at the voluntary or statutory small-corporate audit level; USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 for a larger company crossing the KRW 12 billion asset threshold.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.4% combined statutory headline rate (24% national Corporate Income Tax plus 10% Local Income Tax surcharge on national tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean tax law does not provide blanket e-commerce tax holidays, but incentives available include Foreign Investment Promotion Act cash grants, Free Economic Zone 5-year/3-year 50% corporate tax reductions for qualifying foreign-invested companies, R&D expense tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, and small/venture SME corporate tax reductions; automated dropshipping resale activities generally qualify only for ordinary expense deductions and limited SME credits if the Chusik Hoesa has eligible Korean employees and minimum functional substance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Standard Tax Base and Final Tax Return Form (Form 1), filed electronically via the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal; accompanied by Financial Statements, Tax Reconciliation Statement, and, for non-resident shareholders, the dividend withholding tax return and treaty relief application schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final filing with semi-annual provisional tax payments during the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: A domestic Chusik Hoesa must file the final corporate income tax return and pay any tax due within 3 months from the close of the fiscal year, e.g., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end; extended filing requires prior permission and does not defer the payment obligation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification heading containing the corporate registration number, company name, representative director, tax office, business address, ISIC industrial code, and date of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Chusik Hoesa Korean corporate registration number; if the company is majority-owned by non-residents, the representative director and foreign shareholder list must align with the corporate register, and any change in foreign shareholding during the year must be reported before filing to avoid mismatch penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year period, number of business months, and financial statement basis under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards or Korean GAAP
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the 12-month period exactly; for automated dropshipping revenue received through Stripe and PayPal, all sales must be recognized gross, not net of payment gateway fees, and foreign payment settlement reports must be reconciled to the revenue schedule

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of total gross income, domestic and foreign sourced revenue, sales returns and allowances, and cost of goods sold traceable from procurement and inventory records
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include dropshipping revenues associated with Korean customers and, where the Chusik Hoesa has Korean enterprise substance, all online sales sourced to Korea; do not net additional digital service fees and record freight and customs duty in cost of goods sold only when title and risk of loss pass before delivery to the Korean customer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, including purchases, logistics, cloud infrastructure, payment processing commissions, marketing, and overhead deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses charged by related-party procurement vendors in tax treaty jurisdictions are subject to transfer pricing adjustment; if the dropshipping seller lacks physical inventory, no imputed inventory cost may be claimed unless actual Korean warehouse or genuine goods ownership is demonstrated; foreign platform payments must be substantiated by contract, invoice, and bank transfer evidence

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reconciliation adjustments covering non-deductible expenses, depreciation book-tax differences, reserve adjustments, entertainment expense limitations, and other taxable income adjustments derived from the Tax Reconciliation Statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrual-basis mismatches between PayPal/Stripe settlement and invoice dates must be added back; penalties apply if non-deductible charges such as excessive head-office fees, personal shareholder expenses, or undocumented foreign payments are eliminated by the tax official rather than self-adjusted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of adjusted taxable income after deduction of prior-year net operating losses, with the schedule of loss carryforward years and amount attached
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred by the same Korean corporate taxpayer may be carried forward; a change in majority ownership combined with a change in business purpose may trigger controlled-foreign-company rules or deny loss inheritance, so non-resident directors must ensure that a pivot into automated dropshipping does not constitute a business termination

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable progressive corporate tax rate calculation showing the national tax amount and Local Income Tax surcharge at 10% of national tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute national tax using the statutory brackets applicable to the tax year and claim small/venture corporate tax reduction only if the Chusik Hoesa satisfies the headcount and turnover criteria; the local surcharge is reported with the corporate return but remitted through the integrated payment system

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayment offsets, including foreign tax credits, interim provisional tax payments, withholding credits, and the non-resident shareholder dividend withholding tax offset
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the dropshipping entity has a foreign branch or foreign permanent establishment, claim source-country withholding taxes via the unilateral foreign tax credit; no credit is available for taxes avoided in a no-tax jurisdiction; every interim payment voucher must be tied out to the National Tax Service receipt number

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International related-party transaction schedule covering sales, purchases, intangible royalties, interest, and service charges with foreign related parties, together with the transfer pricing documentation index
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all cross-border dropshipping procurement, licensing, and delegated marketplace services; if the gross covered international transaction amount reaches the Local File threshold of KRW 10 billion or Master File threshold of KRW 100 billion, attach the documentation because failure to do so exposes the filing to understatement penalties and a 10-year statute-of-limitation extension

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend withholding tax computation on dividends declared to non-resident shareholders, at a 20% national withholding rate plus 2% Local Income Tax, subject to approved treaty relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean payer must withhold before remittance and file/remit the withholding tax by the 10th day of the month following payment; attach an original Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration for each treaty claimant, otherwise withhold at the full 22% statutory rate and pursue a refund claim if the treaty relief application is later approved

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, income statement, notes, and statement of changes in equity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reflect all receivable and payable positions from payment gateway settlement accounts; do not hold offshore funds in nominee accounts; a director who signs financial statements that omit foreign payment processing accounts may be deemed to have submitted a fraudulent return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration page attesting that the return is true and complete, signed by the representative director and/or authorized tax agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean representative director, even if a nominee, personally certifies the return; deliberate false certification can support piercing the corporate veil and criminal prosecution, so non-resident principals should not rely on a shell director signature as separation from liability

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: The National Tax Service Framework Act and Corporate Tax Act impose additional taxes of 20% of the understated tax for unfiled returns, 10% of the deficiency for ordinary underreporting, 40% of the deficiency for fraudulent concealment, daily late-payment surcharges of approximately 0.022% per day, and, under the Statute on Punishment of Tax Evaders, imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to five times the evaded tax; failure to attach transfer pricing documentation also attracts separate administrative fines and extends the assessment period to 10 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% Local Income Tax on dividends, producing a combined statutory withholding rate of 22% before bilateral treaty relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced Korean dividend withholding under an applicable Double Tax Treaty, the foreign beneficial-owner shareholder must: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate for the dividend payment year; (2) file the National Tax Service application for treaty exemption/reduction before or with the withholding remittance deadline; (3) provide a beneficial ownership declaration proving the right to receive, control, and dispose of the dividend and absence of a conduit arrangement; (4) satisfy the treaty's ownership threshold and minimum holding period, commonly 25% or more for a 12-month period where a reduced rate is available; and (5) obtain the tax authority's approval decision before remittance; if treaty relief is not approved in time, the payer must withhold at 22% and the shareholder may file an amended refund claim or invoke the mutual agreement procedure under the treaty
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest to non-residents is 20% national plus 2% Local Income Tax, i.e., 22% gross, reduced by applicable DTA rates which generally range from 0% to 15% for interest and 5% to 15% for royalties depending on beneficial ownership, treaty wording, and domestic anti-abuse conditions; excessive related-party royalties may also be recharacterized as non-deductible constructive dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and supporting transfer pricing documentation must be prepared when annual international related-party transactions exceed KRW 10 billion; Master File is required where consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion, and Country-by-Country Report is mandatory when consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion; all thresholds are expressed in Korean won before VAT
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the treaty anti-conduit beneficial-ownership rule, so the Chusik Hoesa must demonstrate substantive core income-generating activities in Korea, including order management, customer service, strategic procurement, platform control, payment settlement judgment, and risk assumption; although standalone Economic Substance Regulations of the UAE type are not separately enacted in Korea, income attribution and permanent establishment standards under the OECD framework equally require the Korean entity to show real staff, premises, and decision-making substance, otherwise it may be disregarded as a shell or invoice-through company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately using non-Korean registered PayPal/Stripe accounts, overseas nominee receiving accounts, or unregistered automated marketplace storefronts to collect dropshipping revenues, failing to issue invoices, understating gross sales, destroying the sales reconciliation audit trail, or omitting foreign payment gateway receipts for the purpose of avoiding corporate income tax and value added tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 3 of the Statute on Punishment of Tax Evaders, aggravated tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding five times the evaded tax; the National Tax Service will additionally assess a 40% fraudulent underreporting penalty, the 10% Local Income Tax surcharge, daily late-payment interest, and may deny the use of loss carryforwards to shelter concealed income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the Chusik Hoesa's veil when the company is a mere instrument of the non-resident principal and directors sign false returns while commingling personal and corporate PayPal/Stripe proceeds; the representative director faces personal civil liability to the revenue authority, vulnerability to asset seizure and NTS travel-ban blacklisting, and criminal imprisonment for false declarations; directors involved in funneling undisclosed sales to a foreign controlling shareholder are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, penalties, and interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Sham Procurement Structure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa purchases goods and logistics services exclusively from a related-party foreign entity in a low-tax or no-tax e-commerce hub at inflated markups, processing fees, or license charges, with no actual price negotiation, no risk-bearing capacity, and no independent supplier selection authority, leaving the Korean entity a residual commission while reporting minimal or loss-making Korean taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may adjust taxable income to the arm's length result under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, add a 30% transfer pricing adjustment penalty, disallow the non-arm's length expense, impose ordinary understatement penalties of 20% to 40% for omitted controlled transaction schedules, and deny management charges as non-deductible; unpaid adjusted tax triggers collection enforcement, travel blacklisting, and criminal referral thresholds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve sham invoices or route inflated markups to shell suppliers are treated as quasi-trustees; they may be personally liable for the adjusted tax difference, statutory surcharges, and interest, their Korean entry/exit can be banned, and if the margin extraction is structured to defraud the tax authority or creditors, criminal investigation for tax evasion can result in imprisonment of the responsible directors notwithstanding the company's separate legal personality.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Abuse on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Chusik Hoesa as a treaty-shopping conduit by routing dividends, interest, or royalties to an intermediate holding company in a third jurisdiction having a favorable DTA with Korea, where the intermediate entity lacks real economic activity, has no independent authority, immediately on-passes the funds, or submits fabricated Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial ownership declarations to claim reduced withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service will deny treaty benefits under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule and beneficial ownership requirements, reassess the full 22% withholding tax plus interest, impose a 40% fraudulent understatement additional tax, and refer the matter for criminal prosecution under the Statute on Punishment of Tax Evaders where wilful false statements are made; the Korean payer's failure to withhold also makes the Chusik Hoesa and its managing director jointly liable for the unreported withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the veil of the Korean operating company exposes the representative director to withholding-agent joint liability, civil asset restitution, travel-ban blacklisting of responsible directors, freezing of personal bank accounts, and, where the concealed withholding tax exceeds the criminal threshold, imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to five times the tax shortfall.
